svg.text: The child on chemotherapy: fever is the emergency
The treatment removes the defences, so ordinary organisms become lethal
A fever in a neutropenic child
Antibiotics within the hour, after cultures — do not wait for the blood count to return
There may be no pus, no redness and no swelling, because there are no cells to make them
So the fever may be the only sign that exists. Treat it as the whole picture.
Daily nursing that prevents admission
Scrupulous hand hygiene by everyone
Mouth care — ulcers are a route in and a
reason the child stops eating
No live vaccines, no unwell visitors
Watch the line site, and record every temperature
Avoid the rectal route entirely
Talking to the child, by age
Under five: fears separation and pain, not death
School age: wants to know if it will hurt, and
often believes the illness is a punishment
Adolescent: hair loss and being different can
matter more to her than the prognosis
Ask what she thinks is happening first
Why childhood cancer is often found late in Ghana
The early signs are ordinary: a limp, a swelling, pallor, a squint, a fever that keeps returning
Families try several treatments before reaching a hospital that can diagnose it
Treatment is abandoned more often than it fails — ask about transport and money early
